content: ToxMystery is an educational program specifically designed for children aged 7 to 11 years. This activity aims to teach young learners about environmental hazards that may exist in their homes. It not only helps them identify these hazards but also educates them on how to make their homes safer. The program is guided by an animated character named Toxie, a cat who provides information in an engaging manner and rewards participants with fun incentives. ToxMystery was developed by the United States National Library of Medicine (NLM) to address the need for greater awareness of household hazards among children in the K-6 age range. Recognizing the lack of environmental health resources tailored for children, the NLM created a user-friendly interface featuring a memorable character to deliver critical information in an entertaining and educational way. In addition to its online version, ToxMystery is also available on a CD-ROM, which can be distributed to teachers. The program includes lesson plans and classroom activities designed to complement the educational experience. To play ToxMystery, users need either the CD-ROM version (provided in limited release to educators) or access to the internet with the latest version of Macromedia Flash Player. The game begins when the player clicks on the front door of Toxie’s house. If instructions are needed, a “getting started” guide is available in the bottom menu. The objective of the game is to identify all environmental health hazards within the house. Players navigate through the house by moving the cursor across different rooms and clicking to explore them. Within each room, players search for animated “hot spots” that indicate hidden chemical hazards. Clicking on these hot spots triggers a question about the specific location and the potential chemical hazard present. If the player answers incorrectly, a brief explanation is provided, and they are allowed to try again. Correct answers earn the player a “paw print,” enabling them to progress further. Once all paw prints in a room are collected, the room is considered complete, and Toxie rewards the player with an animated movie. After completing the entire house, Toxie presents the player with a printable certificate of completion. The goals of ToxMystery extend beyond educating K-6 learners. The program also aims to support parents and teachers by providing them with appropriate resources on environmental health. Parents can access the “Parent Resources” tab to find links to other NLM projects and pages. The “Teacher’s Resources” section includes comprehensive lesson plans centered around ToxMystery, along with worksheets and creative activities for students, such as coloring and crafting exercises.
